The 2025 SC1040TC describes credit code 060 as 'For full-year resident individuals who claimed the Earned Income Tax Credit on their federal return. (TC-60)', and the TC-60 itself instructs the taxpayer to STOP (no credit) if they were not a full-year SC resident or were not eligible for the federal EITC.

_strings.@@3578f028c564: 2025 SC1040 Individual Income Tax Instructions (August 2025), Before You Begin: 'South Carolina conforms to the Internal Revenue Code as amended through December 31, 2024, except as otherwise provided.' — 'These instructions reflect the law as of the end of the 2025 South Carolina legislative session.'
_strings.@@4be354178cac: Treaty conformity — SC conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from SC income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the SC return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: SC1040 line 1 starts from FEDERAL TAXABLE INCOME ('Enter your taxable income from your federal form. If your federal taxable income is zero or less, enter zero here and enter your negative amount on line r' - 2025 SC1040 instructions, Line 1; the 2025 SC1040 form itself prints 'Enter federal taxable income from your federal form'). Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal taxable income before the SC return begins. SC's additions to income (SC1040 lines a-e) do NOT include any add-back of tax-treaty-exempt income. The only foreign-related add-back is on line e ('Add back foreign area allowances, cost of living allowances, and income from US possessions' - 2025 SC1040 instructions, Line e), which is distinct from income exempt under a federal income tax treaty and does not re-capture treaty income. Because treaty-exempt income is neither in the federal taxable-income starting point nor added back, it is NOT re-taxed by SC -> conforms. (SC conforms to the IRC as amended through December 31, 2024, except as otherwise provided.)

The 2025 SC1040 instructions reflect the law as of the end of the 2025 South Carolina session, before the federal act of July 4, 2025 (P.L. 119-21) that created the 2025 deductions for tips, overtime, car-loan interest and seniors. SC1040 line 1 starts from federal taxable income, and the instructions do not say how those deductions are treated. Confirm with SCDOR before relying on a federal taxable income that includes them. _strings.@@94a37bf1aa56: Child and Dependent Care Credit — Full-year SC residents who incurred federal child and dependent care expenses (reported on federal Form 2441). Part-year residents/nonresidents are not eligible if they are residents of a state that does not offer a credit for child and dependent care expense to nonresidents of that state; an eligible part-year resident/nonresident computes the credit on the prorated federal expense using the Schedule NR proration percentage. Cannot be claimed if filing status is Married Filing Separately.
_strings.@@9964157f0bc9: Two Wage Earner Credit — Married couples filing jointly when both spouses have earned income taxed to South Carolina. Not allowed for filing statuses Single, Married Filing Separately, or Head of Household. If either spouse's qualified earned income is zero or less, the credit cannot be taken.
_strings.@@c503406f45d7: Schedule NR (Nonresident Schedule), attached to a completed SC1040. Nonresidents and part-year residents electing to file as a nonresident complete Schedule NR; Column A = income from the federal return, Column B = income earned while an SC resident or from SC sources. The 2025 SC1040 instructions, Line 1: 'STOP! If you are a nonresident/part-year filer, you must complete the Schedule NR and go to line 5.'

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: 2025 Form SC1040, line 6: 'TAX on your South Carolina Income Subject to Tax (see SC1040TT)'. Line 5 (South Carolina Income Subject to Tax) = line 1 federal taxable income ('Enter federal taxable income from your federal form') + line 2 SC additions (lines a-e) - line 4 SC subtractions (lines f-w, including the line w dependent exemption this block ships). This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: TY2025 RATE STEP-DOWN: the top rate fell from 6.2% to 6% (the annual Act 228 of 2022 reduction toward 6%; the 2025 SC1040TT's $100,000-or-more schedule prints 'Multiply the amount on line 5 by 6%'), the bracket bounds indexed to $3,560/$17,830 (from $3,460/$17,330), the subtraction constants became $107/$642 (from $104/$659), and the line w dependent exemption rose to $4,930 (from $4,790). Base guidance: supply SC1040 line 5 (South Carolina Income Subject to Tax) BEFORE the line w dependent exemption — i.e. line 1 federal TAXABLE income (federal 1040 line 15; the federal standard/itemized deduction is already embedded, never subtract it again) plus SC additions (lines a-e) minus the other SC subtractions (lines f-v) — and pass dependents_count so the op subtracts the shipped $4,930-per-dependent line w amount to reproduce line 5. South Carolina has NO personal exemption and NO state standard deduction of its own. Adjudication note (two-pass): pass 1 = the 2025 SC1040TT, Revised 6/17/25 (mandatory tables below $100,000 + the printed $100,000-or-more schedule '6% minus $642', example $101,000 -> $5,418); pass 2 = the 2025 SC4972's printed '2025 Tax Computation Schedule for Line 19 and Line 22' ($0-$3,560 0%; $3,560-$17,830 3% times the amount minus $107; $17,830 or more 6% times the amount minus $642). Both passes agree on every bound and rate, and the tables' own band arithmetic independently pins the bounds (the $3,600-$3,650 row prints $2 = 3% x $3,625 - $107 rounded; the increment per $100 row switches from $3 to $6 across the $17,830 boundary). NOTE: the SC1040 instruction booklet itself prints NO bracket dollar bounds — the SC4972 schedule is the official in-form statement of them. CRITICAL — SC's filed arithmetic is a SUBTRACTION METHOD, not marginal accumulation: the official computation is 'rate x ENTIRE income - constant', and the printed constants are ROUNDED (2025: $107 vs the exact marginal $106.80; $642 vs the exact $641.70 — note the top constant is now rounded AGAINST the taxpayer by 30 cents, the reverse of 2024's $659-vs-$658.36). Pure marginal accumulation (this engine) therefore comes out up to ~$1 LOWER than 2024's relationship above $17,830 and, for 2025, agrees with the SC1040TT's own printed $100,000-or-more example to the dollar ($101,000: engine $5,418.30 -> $5,418; printed 6% x $101,000 - $642 = $5,418). Inside the 3% band the engine is up to 20 cents higher than the filed formula. The filed return must still use the SC1040TT table or the $100,000+ schedule; treat this block's output as an estimate within ~$1-3 (table bands add their own few-dollar spread). Tax-table mandate: taxable income under $100,000 MUST use the SC1040TT tax tables (2025 SC1040 instructions, Line 6); the tables are built in $50/$100 bands from the subtraction formulas at band midpoints (rounded), so a row can differ from exact arithmetic by a few dollars in either direction (e.g. exact $17,830 -> engine $428, but the $17,800-$17,900 row prints $429). Taxable income of $100,000 or more MUST use the rate schedule (6% x line 5 - $642). ONE rate schedule for every filing status — the 2025 SC1040TT states 'Use this Tax Rate Schedule for any filing status claimed on the SC1040'; the identical schedule is duplicated across all four statuses here, copied, not derived (qualifying surviving spouse included). Zero-rate floor: the first $3,560 of SC taxable income is taxed at 0% (the schema's zero-rate bottom bracket, like OH/MS) — a filer at or below $3,560 owes $0 with no exemption needed. Credits are NOT modeled (tax credits, not base reductions): Two Wage Earner Credit (line 12, .007 x up to $50,000 of the lower-earning spouse's qualified earned income, max $350), Child and Dependent Care Credit (line 11, 7% of the federal expense, max $210/$420), SC Earned Income Tax Credit (125% of the federal EITC via TC-60 -> SC1040TC code 060 -> line 13, nonrefundable), and the refundable Tuition Tax Credit (line 21, Form I-319, 50% up to $1,500). Out of scope on the same return: TAX on Lump-Sum Distribution (line 7, SC4972) is a separate additional tax; Active Trade or Business income electing the flat rate (Form I-335, line 8) is excluded from this schedule; the 2.5% additional tax on excess catastrophe-savings withdrawals (line 9) is separate too — all are computed on their own forms.
